commit.message:
fix(cat): name unpacked inputs by where they came from, not their temp file (#4782)

* fix(cat): name unpacked inputs by where they came from, not their temp file

`cat rowskey --group` took its values from the files process_input
unpacked into a temp dir, so a folder per month each holding
data.csv.sz gave `.tmpXXXX/data.csv` and `dup1/data.csv` under
parentdirfname, and `fullpath` gave a temp path for every unpacked
input.

process_input_with_sources now also returns where each path came from
(stdin, a file, a .sz file, or a zip entry); process_input wraps it, so
no other caller changes. cat names each input as if unpacked in place:
jan/data.csv.sz as jan/data.csv, entry data.csv in feb/mar.zip as
feb/mar/data.csv (what parentdirfname already gave for zips; fname and
fstem are unchanged). Stdin gives `<stdin>` for fullpath and
`stdin.csv` for the parentdir kinds. Errors and warnings name an
unpacked input as given (jan/data.csv.sz, feb/mar.zip/data.csv).

Fixes #4781

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(changelog): cite #4782

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(cat): --group fullpath names the real file for compressed inputs

The in-place name `jan/data.csv` for `jan/data.csv.sz` is right for the
parentdir and fname kinds, but under `fullpath` it named a file that
may not exist, or a different one: `jan/data.csv` and `jan/data.csv.sz`
both gave `/…/jan/data.csv`. `fullpath` now names the real source:
`/…/jan/data.csv.sz`, and `/…/feb/mar.zip/data.csv` for a zip entry
(the form errors already use). Other kinds are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(changelog): note that same-named zips share a parentdirfname

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(cat): build parentdirfname expectations with MAIN_SEPARATOR

The #4781 .sz and zip grouping tests hard-coded `/` in the
parentdirfname values they expect; get_parentdir_and_file joins with
Path::join, so Windows CI would see backslashes. Same pattern as the
existing parentdir tests.

Addresses roborev 5195 and 5197.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

files.patch:
@@ -30,6 +30,7 @@ and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0
   - Building qsv from source now also patches `hashbrown` to Polars' fork (the same pin Polars itself uses), because Polars 2.0 relies on prefetch APIs that aren't in a hashbrown release yet ([rust-lang/hashbrown#727](https://github.com/rust-lang/hashbrown/pull/727)).
 
 ### Fixed
+- **`cat` names compressed and piped inputs by where they came from, not by a temp file** ([#4781](https://github.com/dathere/qsv/issues/4781), [#4782](https://github.com/dathere/qsv/pull/4782)). `cat` unpacks `.sz` and `.zip` inputs and piped stdin into a temp directory, and `cat rowskey --group` took its values from those temp files. So `--group parentdirfname` over a folder per month, each holding `data.csv.sz`, gave `.tmpXXXX/data.csv` and `dup1/data.csv` instead of `jan/data.csv` and `feb/data.csv`, and `--group fullpath` gave a temp path for every unpacked input. `fullpath` now names the real file: `/…/jan/data.csv.sz`, or `/…/feb/mar.zip/data.csv` for an entry `data.csv` in `feb/mar.zip`. The other kinds name an unpacked input as if it were unpacked in place, so `parentdirfname` gives `jan/data.csv` for `jan/data.csv.sz` and `mar/data.csv` for the zip entry. That is already what it gave for zip entries, and `fname`/`fstem` are unchanged. Because a zip archive stands in for its folder, same-named archives in sibling folders (`jan/data.zip` and `feb/data.zip`, each holding `data.csv`) still share a `parentdirfname` (`data/data.csv`); use `--group fullpath` to tell them apart. Piped stdin gives `<stdin>` for `fullpath` and `stdin.csv` for the parentdir kinds (it was `.tmpXXXX/stdin.csv`). `cat`'s error messages and warnings now name an unpacked input as given (`jan/data.csv.sz`, or `feb/mar.zip/data.csv` for a zip entry) instead of its bare decompressed name.
 - **Same-named compressed inputs no longer overwrite each other** ([#4779](https://github.com/dathere/qsv/issues/4779), [#4780](https://github.com/dathere/qsv/pull/4780)). Commands that take several inputs (`cat`, `headers`, `sqlp`, `to`, `validate`, `slice`, `lens`, `tojsonl`, `describegpt`, `scoresql`) unpack `.sz` and `.zip` inputs into a temp directory, named for the input alone. Two inputs with the same name, such as `jan/data.csv.sz` and `feb/data.csv.sz` or `jan/data.zip` and `feb/data.zip`, were unpacked to the same place, so one file's data was silently lost and the other's was read twice. Piped stdin and a file named `stdin.csv.sz` clashed the same way, and so did `joinp`'s two inputs when both were same-named `.sz` files (the join read the right-hand file twice). Each input now keeps its own data. Unpacked file names are unchanged, but **with `validate --split-ragged`, the second of two same-named inputs now writes its split files under `dup1/` in the current directory** (e.g. `dup1/data.csv.valid`), where before both inputs wrote to the same `data.csv.*` files.
 - **`cat rows` stops cleanly on a record of the wrong length, and says where it is** ([#4778](https://github.com/dathere/qsv/pull/4778)). Without `--flexible`, a record wider or narrower than the ones before it was half-written to the output (its fields, with no line ending) before the error, and the error named neither the file nor, for a mismatch between files, the line. The width is now checked before each record is written, so the output ends at the last good record, and the error reads like `` `sales.csv` line 2: found a record with 3 fields, but the records before it have 2 ``. Piped input is named `<stdin>`.
 - **`cat` no longer loses data in two edge cases** ([#4777](https://github.com/dathere/qsv/pull/4777)).
